367127.title: Recolouring conjecture for odd-hole-free graphs
367127.statement:
Let $G$ be an odd-hole-free graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ and clique number $\omega$. A proper colouring is **Kempe-recolourable** when it can be transformed through Kempe changes, which interchange two colours on a connected component of the corresponding bichromatic subgraph.

**Odd-hole-free recolouring conjecture.** All odd-hole-free graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$ and clique number $\omega$ are $k$-recolourable for

$$
k \geqslant \left\lceil \frac{\omega + \Delta + 1}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

This is motivated by known Kempe-recolouring results for odd-hole-free graphs, which rule out the main known frozen-colouring obstruction above the local Reed threshold. The conjectured full recolourability at this sharper bound remains open.

367135.title: Euclidean distortion conjecture for finite subsets of $L_p$
367135.statement:
For $n\to\finity$ and $p>2$, let $\mathsf{c}_2^n(L_p)$ denote the maximum, over all $n$-point metric spaces, of the least distortion with which the space embeds into $L_p$ and then into Euclidean space. The known bounds give $\mathsf{c}_2^n(L_p)=o(\log n)$ when $p=o\big(\sqrt[6]{\log n}/\sqrt[3]{\log\log n}\big)$, while $\mathsf{c}_2^n(L_p)\asymp\log n$ when $p\gtrsim\log n$. **Euclidean distortion conjecture.** One should have

$$
\mathsf{c}_2^n(L_p)=o(\log n)
$$

in the remaining range

$$
\sqrt[6]{\log n}/\sqrt[3]{\log\log n}\lesssim p=o(\log n).
$$

This would determine the qualitative Euclidean distortion growth throughout the currently unresolved intermediate range; the endpoint regimes are supplied by the theorem and by the embedding of $\ell_\infty^n$ into $L_p$.

367140.title: Unimodality conjecture for Toda eigenfunction numerators
367140.statement:
For $\alpha\in Q^{\geq 0}$, let $\mathfrak{J}_\alpha$ be the Toda eigenfunction and let $(q)_\alpha$ be the associated $q$-factorial. A polynomial is **unimodal** if its coefficient sequence weakly increases to a maximum and then weakly decreases. **Unimodality conjecture.** The polynomial

$$
(q)_\alpha^2\mathfrak{J}_\alpha
$$

is unimodal. This is motivated by empirical observations after the positivity conjecture; the source gives no proof or resolution.

367170.title: Finite monoid catenary degree for conductor submonoids
367170.statement:
Let $F$ be a factorial monoid and let $H\subset F$ be a **conductor submonoid**. The **reduced monoid** $F_{\mathrm{red}}$ is obtained by factoring out the units of $F$.

**Finite catenary-degree conjecture.** If $F_{\mathrm{red}}$ is finitely generated, then

$$
\mathsf c_{\mathrm{mon}}(H)<\infty.
$$

The conjecture asks whether finite generation of the reduced factorial ambient monoid forces the monoid catenary degree of every conductor submonoid to be finite. The surrounding results establish restrictions on adjacent catenary degrees and construct examples with arbitrarily large equal-length catenary degree, but do not resolve this finiteness question.

367199.title: The prime-characterization conjecture for the maximum cycle-displacement function
367199.statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group on $n$ elements, let $C_n$ denote the cyclic-shift subgroup, and let $t(n)$ be the function defined in the paper by the maximum, over $\tau\in S_n$, of the minimum of $n-\operatorname{cyc}(\sigma)$ for $\sigma\in\tau C_n$.

**Prime-characterization conjecture.**

$$
t(n)=n-2 \quad\text{if and only if}\quad n\text{ is prime}.
$$

The equality is proved when $n$ is prime; the converse remains conjectural in the source.

367202.title: Coxeter code distance conjecture
367202.statement:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system of rank $m$. For an integer $r$, let 
$$
be the Coxeter code generated by standard cosets of rank $m-r$, and let
$$
 denote its distance.

**Coxeter code distance conjecture.** The distance is

$$
\operatorname{dist}(\mathcal{C}_{W}(r))=\min_{J\subseteq S,\ |J|=m-r}\left|\langle J\rangle\right|.
$$

The right-hand side is the trivial upper bound obtained from the smallest standard coset of rank $m-r$; the conjecture asserts that this bound is attained.

367219.title: Adjusted tensor-product conjecture for Macaulay rings
367219.statement: Let $S$ be a Macaulay ring, let $x$ be a variable not appearing in $S$, and let $n$ be strictly larger than the largest degree of any element of $S$. **Adjusted tensor-product conjecture.** Then $S\otimes_K K[x]/(x^n)$ is a Macaulay ring. The authors report that they found no counterexamples to this adjusted version, but the supplied text does not establish that it has been proved or otherwise resolved.

367243.title: Twisted arithmetic transfer conjecture for regular semisimple intersections
367243.statement:
Let $L_0=\mathbb Z_p^n$ and $L_0^\vee=p^{-1}\mathbb Z_p^t\oplus\mathbb Z_p^{n-t}$, and let $\mathrm{GL}(L_0,L_0^\vee)$ be the corresponding parahoric subgroup. For a regular semisimple pair $(g,u)\in(\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb V)/\mathrm U(\mathbb V)\times\mathbb V)(\mathbb Q_p)_{\mathrm{rs}}$, let $\mathrm {Int}^{\mathrm {Herm},\mathbb V}(g,u)$ be the derived intersection number defined in the supplied context. For a matching regular semisimple triple $(\gamma,u_1,u_2)\in(\mathrm {GL}_n(\mathbb Q_p)\times\mathbb Q_p^n\times(\mathbb Q_p^n)^*)_{\mathrm{rs}}$, let $\mathrm{Orb}$ be the twisted orbital integral defined there. **Twisted arithmetic transfer conjecture.** For every such matching pair and triple,

$$
\mathrm {Int}^{\mathrm {Herm},\mathbb V}(g,u)\log p=-\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}\mathrm {Orb}\left((\gamma,u_1,u_2),1_{\mathrm {GL}(L_0,L_0^\vee)}\times1_{L_0}\times1_{(L_0^\vee)^*},s\right)\in\mathbb Q\log p.
$$

This is an arithmetic transfer identity comparing derived intersection numbers on a unitary Rapoport--Zink space with derivatives of twisted orbital integrals; the supplied text gives no resolution of the conjecture.

367262.title: The omega-categoricity conjecture for second-order strongly minimal sets
367262.statement:
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a strongly minimal set of differential order $2$ definable over the field of constants $\mathcal{C}$. A set is **$\omega$-categorical** if, for every non-constant solution $x\in\mathcal{X}$, the set $\mathcal{C}\langle x\rangle^{\mathrm{alg}}\cap\mathcal{X}$ is finite. For distinct non-constant solutions $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ satisfying

$$
\operatorname{tr.deg}_{\mathcal{C}}\mathcal{C}\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n\rangle=2n,
$$

**The $\omega$-categoricity conjecture.** The set $\mathcal{X}$ is $\omega$-categorical if and only if there is a positive integer $k$ such that, for every such tuple $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, all but $kn$ other non-constant solutions $x$ satisfy

$$
\operatorname{tr.deg}_{\mathcal{C}}\mathcal{C}\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n,x\rangle=2n+2.
$$

This conjecture concerns the proposed characterization of finite algebraic dependence among solutions of second-order strongly minimal differential equations. In the stated source, the general conjecture is disproved by a counterexample of Freitag and Scanlon arising from the third-order differential equation satisfied by the $j$-function.

367281.title: Polylogarithmic non-giant components conjecture for the square graph
367281.statement:
Let $[?]$ be an Erdős–Rényi random graph, $[?][?]$, and let $[?]([?])$ be the auxiliary square graph. Let $[?]>0$ be fixed, and write $[?]$ for a quantity bounded above and below by positive powers of $[?]$.

**Polylogarithmic non-giant components conjecture.** Suppose

$$
p=p(n)\geq \frac{\sqrt{\sqrt{6}-2}+\varepsilon}{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

Then a.a.s. every connected component of $[?]([?])$ except the largest has size $([?])^{O(1)}$.

This is a concluding open question about the component structure at and above the predicted giant-square-component threshold. The paper's theorem establishes a related polylogarithmic bound in a range beginning at a larger order, while this conjecture aims at the earlier threshold.

367331.title: The F-conjecture for moduli spaces of stable curves
367331.statement: Let $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}$ be the moduli space of stable curves, and let an **F-curve** be a one-dimensional codimension-$3g-4+n$ boundary stratum. A line bundle is F-nef if it has nonnegative intersection with every F-curve, and F-ample if it has positive intersection with every F-curve. **F-conjecture.** A line bundle on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}$ is nef if and only if it is F-nef. Equivalently, it is ample if and only if it is F-ample. This conjecture would completely determine the F-cone of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}$; the source attributes it to Gibney, Keel, and Morrison and says it is a conjecture, without giving a resolution.

367356.title: Nguyen–Scott–Seymour conjecture on additive quasi-isometries to bounded-tree-width graphs
367356.statement:
A graph is **quasi-isometric** to another graph if there is a quasi-isometry between their metric spaces; a quasi-isometry with **additive distortion** has bounded additive error in distances. The **tree-width** of a graph is the minimum width of a tree-decomposition of the graph.

**Nguyen–Scott–Seymour conjecture.** There is a constant $k$ such that if a graph $G$ admits a quasi-isometry to a graph of tree-width at most two, then $G$ admits a quasi-isometry with additive distortion to a graph of tree-width at most $k$.

This conjecture asks whether quasi-isometry to graphs of tree-width two can always be improved to a quasi-isometry with only additive distortion while retaining bounded tree-width. The supplied context presents it as a conjecture and does not state a resolution.

367363.title: Furtula–Oz conjecture on extremal complementary second Zagreb graphs
367363.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices, and let $cM_{2}(G)$ denote its complementary second Zagreb index, defined by

$$
cM_{2}(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\left|d_{G}(u)^{2}-d_{G}(v)^{2}\right|.
$$

Here $K_m\vee\overline{K_{n-m}}$ is the join of the complete graph on $m$ vertices and the edgeless graph on $n-m$ vertices. **Furtula–Oz conjecture.** The graph with $n$ vertices and the maximum complementary second Zagreb index is isomorphic to $K_m\vee\overline{K_{n-m}}$ for some $1\leq m\leq n-1$.
This conjecture identifies the proposed extremal structure for the complementary second Zagreb index among graphs of order $n$.

367398.title: Linear bound for the treewidth contraction function
367398.statement:
Let $p,q\geqslant 1$ be integers. Define $\ell(p,q)$ to be the minimum integer such that every graph $G$ with treewidth at least $\ell(p,q)$ contains pairwise disjoint connected subgraphs $G_1,G_2,\dots,G_n$, each with $\operatorname{tw}(G_i)\geqslant p$, and contracting each of $G_1,\dots,G_n$ to a vertex produces a minor of $G$ with treewidth at least $q$. **Proposed bound.**

$$
\ell(p,q)\leqslant O^\ast(pq).
$$

The grid-minor theorem currently gives the weaker bound $\ell(p,q)\leqslant O^\ast((pq)^9)$: a $(pq)\times(pq)$ grid can be partitioned into $q^2$ copies of the $p\times p$ grid, whose contractions yield a $q\times q$ grid. Improving this polynomial bound is posed as an open problem.

367420.title: Minimum-edge bound for k-edge-proper graphs
367420.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, where $k\geq 4$ and $n$ is sufficiently large. A graph is **$k$-edge-proper** if it contains cycles of every length from $k$ through $n$. **Minimum-edge conjecture for $k$-edge-proper graphs.** If $G$ is $k$-edge-proper, then

$$
e(G)\geq \left\lceil\frac{(4k-9)n}{2k-4}\right\rceil.
$$
The bound is supported by a symmetric fan-graph construction that is asymptotically sharp for orders divisible by $2k-4$.

367427.title: The nilpotency-index bound for four-dimensional ${\cal N}=2$ SCFTs
367427.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{rank}$ be the complex dimension of the Coulomb branch of a four-dimensional ${\cal N}=2$ SCFT. Let $\mathfrak{n}$ be the smallest positive integer such that the VOA stress tensor satisfies $T^{\mathfrak{n}}=0$ in the VOA's $C_2$ algebra. **Nilpotency-index bound.** The invariants satisfy

$$
\mathfrak{rank}\leq\mathfrak{n}-1.
$$

The bound would make ordering SCFTs by nilpotency index more refined than ordering them by rank. The source reports saturation for rank-zero theories and gives examples with rank one, but does not establish the conjecture in general.

367451.title: The sphericity conjecture for dichotomous ordinal complete graphs
367451.statement:
Let $\mathrm{pdd}(n)$ denote the minimum dimension required to realize a dichotomous ordinal complete graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\mathrm{sp}(G)$ be the sphericity of a graph $G$, namely the least dimension in which $G$ has a unit ball representation. Write $K_{a,b}$ for the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes $a$ and $b$. **Sphericity conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{pdd}(n)=\mathrm{sp}(K_{\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil,\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor}).
$$

The complete bipartite graph is a dichotomous ordinal graph and therefore gives a lower bound for $\mathrm{pdd}(n)$. The conjecture asserts that the balanced complete bipartite graph is the most difficult such graph to realize, but the source reports no results establishing it.

367452.title: Cyclic edge-connectivity conjecture for cages
367452.statement:
A **$(k,g)$-cage** is a smallest $k$-regular graph of girth $g$. A cycle-separating edge-cut is an edge-cut whose removal yields at least two components containing a cycle. A graph is **cyclically $r$-edge-connected** if it has no cycle-separating edge-cut of fewer than $r$ edges.

**Cyclic edge-connectivity conjecture.** Every $(k,g)$-cage is cyclically $(k-2)g$-edge-connected.

The value $(k-2)g$ is a natural upper bound, obtained by separating a $g$-cycle from the rest of the cage. The source presents this as an open conjecture and proposes it as the maximal possible cyclic edge-connectivity of cages.

367453.title: Cycle-separating cut conjecture for cages
367453.statement:
A **$(k,g)$-cage** is a smallest $k$-regular graph of girth $g$. A cycle-separating edge-cut is an edge-cut whose removal yields at least two components containing a cycle; a $g$-cycle is a cycle of length $g$.

**Cycle-separating cut conjecture.** For each $(k,g)$-cage $G$, every cycle-separating edge-cut of size $(k-2)g$ in $G$ separates a $g$-cycle.

This is presented as a strengthening of the conjectured maximal cyclic edge-connectivity of cages. Its resolution is not indicated in the source.

367480.title: The extremal size conjecture for resilient 3-graphs
367480.statement:
A **2-resilient 3-graph** is a 3-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal{T}$ for which deleting any set of at most two vertices does not decrease its matching number. Let $\nu(\mathcal{T})$ denote the maximum number of pairwise disjoint edges. **The resilient 3-graph conjecture.** If $\mathcal{T}$ is a 2-resilient 3-graph with $\nu(\mathcal{T})=s$, then

$$
|\mathcal{T}|\leq\binom{3s+2}{3}.
$$

This conjecture is the $k=3$ case of the paper's resilient-hypergraph extremal problem; the paper's main result establishes it for $s=2$, while the general statement is not resolved here.

367481.title: The asymptotic extremal-size conjecture for resilient hypergraphs
367481.statement:
Let $m(k,s)$ denote the maximum number of edges in a $(k-1)$-resilient $k$-uniform hypergraph with matching number $s$. **Resilient hypergraph extremal conjecture.** For fixed $k\geq4$ and $s\geq s_0(k)$,

$$
m(k,s)=\binom{ks+k-1}{k}.
$$

The right-hand side is the size of the complete $k$-graph on $ks+k-1$ vertices. The statement is motivated by the absence of better constructions for fixed $k$ and large $s$, whereas the natural construction is not optimal for small $s$; it remains open.

367482.title: The covering-number weakening for resilient hypergraph extremal size
367482.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a $k$-uniform hypergraph, let $\nu(\mathcal{F})$ be its matching number, and let $\tau(\mathcal{F})$ be its covering number, the minimum size of a vertex set meeting every edge. **Resilient hypergraph covering conjecture.** If $\nu(\mathcal{F})=s$ and $\tau(\mathcal{F})=sk$, then, for $s>s_0(k)$,

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leq\binom{sk+k-1}{k}.
$$

This is presented as a weaker version of the preceding conjecture and remains open in the stated range.

367490.title: Lev's matching restricted-sumset conjecture
367490.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime number, and let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p$ with $|B|\leqslant |A|$. Let $\mathcal{R}\colon B\to A$ be an injective function, viewed as a matching between subsets of $A$ and $B$. For the restricted sumset

$$
A+_{\mathcal{R}}B=\{a+b:a\in A,\ b\in B,\ (a,b)\notin\mathcal{R}\},
$$

**Lev's conjecture.**

$$
|A+_{\mathcal{R}}B|\geqslant
\begin{cases}
|A|+|B|-3&\text{if }|A|+|B|\leqslant p,\\
p-3&\text{if }|A|+|B|=p+1,\\
p-2&\text{if }|A|+|B|\geqslant p+2.
\end{cases}
$$

The conjecture concerns the minimum size of a sumset after deleting the pairs specified by a matching; the paper confirms it when $|A|+|B|\leqslant(1-\varepsilon)p$ for sufficiently large $p$, but the full statement remains open.

367491.title: The integer bounded-degree restricted-sumset conjecture
367491.statement:
Let $\Delta\geqslant 1$ be an integer. Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$ satisfy $|B|\leqslant |A|$, and let $\mathcal{R}\subseteq A\times B$ be a binary relation. The **maximum degree on $B$** is the largest number of elements of $A$ related to any single element of $B$. Define

$$
A+_{\mathcal{R}}B=\{a+b:a\in A,\ b\in B,\ (a,b)\notin\mathcal{R}\}.
$$

**Bounded-degree restricted-sumset conjecture.** If the maximum degree of $\mathcal{R}$ on $B$ is at most $\Delta$, then

$$
|A+_{\mathcal{R}}B|\geqslant |A|+|B|-1-\left\lfloor\frac{5\Delta}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

The paper gives constructions attaining this bound, and presents the claim as a conjectural strengthening of its proved estimate; its general validity remains open.

367503.title: The Generalized Two Conjecture for quadratic number fields
367503.statement:
Let $\chi_1$ and $\chi_2$ be nontrivial, primitive Dirichlet characters modulo $q_1$ and $q_2$, respectively, with $\chi_1\chi_2(-1)=1$. Let $F_{\chi_1,\chi_2}$ be the smallest number field containing the values of $\chi_1$ and $\chi_2$, let $\mathbb{Z}[\chi_1,\chi_2]$ denote its ring of integers, and let $S_{\chi_1,\chi_2}$ be the generalized Dedekind sum. **Generalized Two Conjecture.** If $F_{\chi_1,\chi_2}$ is a quadratic number field, then

$$
S_{\chi_1,\chi_2}(\Gamma_1(q_1q_2))=2\mathbb{Z}[\chi_1,\chi_2].
$$

This generalizes the quadratic-character case by allowing the character-value field to be any quadratic number field. The claim is motivated by limited computations and is presented as an open generalization in the supplied source.

367561.title: Roverato's conjecture on G-Wishart normalising constants
367561.statement:
Let $\mathcal G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices. For $D\in\mathbb S^n_{++}$, let $D^{\mathcal G}$ denote the positive-definite completion of $D$ with respect to $\mathcal G$, and let $\operatorname{Iss}_{\mathcal G}(D^{\mathcal G})$ be the corresponding Isserlis matrix. Write $\mathscr C_{\mathcal G}(\delta,D)$ for the $\mathcal G$-Wishart normalising constant and let $I_n$ be the $n\times n$ identity matrix.

**Roverato's conjecture.** For every real number $\delta>0$,

$$
\mathscr C_{\mathcal G}(\delta,D)=2^{\frac n2}\det\!\left(\operatorname{Iss}_{\mathcal G}(D^{\mathcal G})\right)^{-\frac12}\det(D^{\mathcal G})^{-\frac{\delta-2}{2}}\mathscr C_{\mathcal G}(\delta,I_n).
$$

The conjecture would reduce the evaluation of the normalising constant for a general scale matrix to the identity-scale case, with the remaining factors obtainable from positive-definite completion and determinant calculations. It is known for chordal graphs, but the source presents it as unresolved in general.

367605.title: Heinig's Hamilton-generated conjecture for dense balanced bipartite graphs
367605.statement:
Let $G$ be a balanced bipartite graph with $2n$ vertices, and write $\delta(G)$ for its minimum degree. **Heinig's conjecture.** If $n$ is sufficiently large and

$$
\delta(G) \ge \frac{n}{2}+1,
$$

then $G$ is Hamilton-generated, meaning that its cycle space is generated by its Hamiltonian cycles. The source presents this as an interesting problem posed by Heinig; no resolution is supplied there.

367621.title: Eventual stabilization of saturation numbers for finite cycle intervals
367621.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}_I$ denote the family of cycles whose lengths belong to an integer set $I$, and let $\operatorname{sat}(n,\mathcal{C}_I)$ be the minimum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $\mathcal{C}_I$-saturated graph. **The conjecture.** There exist functions $r(s)$ on $s\in[4,+\infty)$ and $n(s,r)$ for $s\in[4,+\infty)$ and $r\in[r(s),+\infty)$ such that for any integers $s\ge4$, $r\ge r(s)$ and $n\ge n(r,s)$,

$$
\operatorname{sat}(n, \mathcal{C}_{[s,r]})=\operatorname{sat}(n, \mathcal{C}_{[s,+\infty)}).
$$

This generalizes the preceding finite-interval conjectures; no resolution is supplied in the source.

367653.title: The c3_{k+1} degree-sum conjecture for 2-factors with at most k cycles
367653.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, let $k$ be a positive integer, and let $c3_{k+1}(G)$ denote the minimum degree sum over every set of $k+1$ pairwise nonadjacent vertices of $G$. **Degree-sum conjecture.** If

$$
c3_{k+1}(G)\geq n
$$

and every independent set $I$ of $G$ satisfies $|I|\leq \u03b4_G(I)-1$, then $G$ has a 2-factor with at most $k$ cycles. This would extend Ore's theorem from a spanning cycle to a 2-factor with a bounded number of cycles under the stated independent-set condition.

367664.title: The packing-coloring conjecture for bounded-degree graphs
367664.statement:
Let $k\geq 3$, and let a **$k$-degree graph** mean a graph of maximum degree at most $k$. A coloring is **$(1^{k-1},2^{k-1},3)$-packing colorable** if its vertices can be partitioned into $k-1$ color classes in which distinct vertices have distance at least $2$, $k-1$ color classes in which distinct vertices have distance at least $3$, and one color class in which distinct vertices have distance at least $4$. **Packing-coloring conjecture.** Every $k$-degree graph is $(1^{k-1},2^{k-1},3)$-packing colorable.

This conjecture refines the known packing-coloring result for subcubic graphs, which are $(1,1,2,2,3)$-packing colorable. The proposed statement concerns all graphs of maximum degree at least three; its resolution is not specified in the source.

367666.title: Avdonin–Zhao's watershed conjecture for optimal graph control time
367666.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a metric graph, and let the free wave equation on $\mathcal{G}$ be observed or controlled from an open subset of the graph. A watershed is the decomposition used by Avdonin and Zhao to determine a control time from the longest river covering the uncontrolled part.

**Avdonin–Zhao's watershed conjecture.** The watershed description of Avdonin and Zhao provides the optimal time for the observation and control of the free wave equation on a graph.

Computing the optimal observation and control time on a general graph is described as an open problem. The watershed time is always shorter than the time obtained from the graph geometric control condition, but its optimality is not known in general.

367680.title: Extremal conjecture for equal-degree endpoint paths of odd length
367680.statement:
Let $p_{\ell}(N)$ denote the maximum number of edges in a graph on $N$ vertices containing no path of length $\ell$ whose endpoints have equal degree. For odd integers $\ell\geq 3$ and sufficiently large positive integers $n$, consider graphs on $2n+1$ vertices; the complete bipartite graph $K_{n,n+1}$ has $n^2+n$ edges.

**Odd-length extremal conjecture.** For any odd integer $\ell\geq 3$ and sufficiently large $n$, it holds that

$$
p_{\ell}(2n+1)=n^2+n.
$$

Equivalently, $K_{n,n+1}$ remains extremal for paths of every odd length at least three. This extends the problem of Erdős and Hajnal on paths with equal-degree endpoints; the asserted extremality is posed as an open problem for general odd lengths.

367708.title: Conjecture on maximizers of the partition discrepancy
367708.statement:
For partitions $\beta$ and $
u$, let $\beta\sqcup\nu$ denote the partition obtained by distributing the parts of $\beta$ and $
u$ among the parts of a partition $\bar\lambda$ of $n$, and let $\Delta(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ be the quantity defined in the source. The maximum of $\Delta(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ over triples with $\lambda\vdash n$, $\mu\vdash n-k$, and $\nu\vdash k$ is attained at a triple of partitions satisfying the following condition.

**Maximizer conjecture.** At most one part of $\lambda$ is the sum of a part in $\mu$ and a part in $\nu$, while the other parts of $\lambda$ are distributed in $\mu$ and $\nu$.

This conjecture proposes a structural description of a maximizer for the discrepancy $\Delta$; the supplied text gives no resolution, so its status remains open.

367713.title: The uniqueness conjecture for symmetric decompositions of 2-admissible I-Gorenstein sequences
367713.statement: Let $A=k[\![x,y]\!]/J$ be an AG $k$-algebra, let $I$ be an ideal in $A$, and let $H$ be a $2$-admissible $G(I)$-Gorenstein sequence. A **symmetric decomposition** is a decomposition of the Hilbert function $H$ into symmetric component sequences. **The uniqueness conjecture.** The symmetric decomposition of $H$ is unique. Symmetric decomposition is known to be determined by the Hilbert function in the codimension-two AG case, but the examples in the paper show that a general $2$-admissible $I$-Gorenstein sequence need not determine its decomposition; the conjecture isolates the case asserted in the source and remains open.

367727.title: Two-cut conjecture for even binary words
367727.statement:
Let $c(W)$ be the minimum integer $c$ such that $W=B_1\cdots B_{c+1}$ can be partitioned into consecutive blocks and, for some permutation $\pi$ of $[c+1]$, the rearranged word $B_{\pi(1)}\cdots B_{\pi(c+1)}$ is a shuffle square. A word is **even** if each letter occurs an even number of times.

**Two-cut conjecture.** Every even binary word $W$ satisfies

$$
c(W)\leqslant 2.
$$

The paper notes that even a bound by an unspecified absolute constant is not known. The analogous claim for ternary words is false, since the paper gives an example with $c(W)=3$.

367728.title: Cutting-distance conjecture for even k-ary words
367728.statement:
For a $k$-ary word $W$, let $c(W)$ be the minimum number of cuts needed to partition $W$ into consecutive blocks that can be permuted to form a shuffle square. A word is **even** if every letter occurs an even number of times.

**Cutting-distance conjecture.** For each $k\geqslant2$, every even $k$-ary word $W$ satisfies

$$
c(W)\leqslant k.
$$

The binary case is posed separately with the stronger bound $c(W)\leqslant2$, while the proposed generalization is compatible with the known ternary example having cutting distance $3$.

367731.title: The asymptotic order conjecture for the Ramsey number r(4,t)
367731.statement:
Let $r(4,t)$ denote the minimum integer $n$ such that every red-blue coloring of the edges of the complete graph on $n$ vertices contains a red copy of $K_4$ or a blue copy of $K_t$. **The $r(4,t)$ order conjecture.** As $t\to\infty$, the order of magnitude of $r(4,t)$ is

$$
\frac{t^3}{(\log t)^2}.
$$

This refines the general lower-bound conjecture in the case $s=4$ and is motivated by the paper's bounds, which determine $r(4,t)$ only up to a factor of order $(\log t)^2$.

367737.title: Prest's conjecture on domestic representation type and Krull-Gabriel dimension
367737.statement:
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field and let $A$ be a finite dimensional algebra over $K$. The **Krull-Gabriel dimension** of $A$, denoted by $\operatorname{KG}(A)$, is the smallest ordinal number $\alpha$ such that the Krull-Gabriel filtration reaches the category of finitely presented functors on finite dimensional $A$-modules, if such an ordinal exists, and is $\infty$ otherwise. **Prest's conjecture.** $A$ is of domestic representation type if and only if

$$
\operatorname{KG}(A)\text{ is finite}.
$$

This conjecture proposes that finite Krull-Gabriel dimension exactly characterizes domestic representation type among finite dimensional algebras. The source attributes it to Prest; no resolution is supplied here.

367742.title: Stein's conjecture on oriented paths in graphs of large semidegree
367742.statement:
Let $G$ be an oriented graph, let $\b7$ denote its minimum semidegree, and let $k$ be a nonnegative integer. An **orientation of the $k$-edge path** is an oriented graph obtained by assigning a direction to each edge of an undirected path with $k$ edges. **Stein's conjecture.** Every oriented graph $G$ with minimum semidegree $\b7(G)>k/2$ contains every orientation of the $k$-edge path.

Jackson's theorem proves the directed-path case. Stein and Trujillo-Negrete proved the conjecture for oriented graphs containing no oriented $4$-cycle, while the general statement remains open; the paper studies two-block paths as a step toward it.

367784.title: Bangachev's minimum-degree conjecture for friends-and-strangers graphs
367784.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be connected graphs on $n$ vertices. For a graph $G$, write $\delta(G)$ for its minimum degree, and let $\operatorname{FS}(X,Y)$ denote the friends-and-strangers graph of $X$ and $Y$. **Bangachev's conjecture.** If

$$
2\min(\delta(X),\delta(Y))+3\max(\delta(X),\delta(Y))\geq 3n,
$$

then $\operatorname{FS}(X,Y)$ is connected. This conjecture concerns minimum-degree conditions guaranteeing connectedness of friends-and-strangers graphs; the supplied text attributes it to Bangachev but gives no evidence of resolution.
